support.quote: The set subcommand modifies the sparse-checkout file with patterns to match the files in the given directories. Further, any files that are immediately in a directory that’s a parent to a specified directory are also included.

For example, if you ran git sparse-checkout set A/B , then Git would include files with names A/B/C.txt (immediate child of A/B ) and A/D.txt (immediate sibling of A/B ) as well as E.txt (immediate sibling of A ).

Given a file path such as /A/B/C/D.txt , Git includes the path in the working directory if any of the following are true: A/B/C is in the parent set, A/B/C is in the recursive set, A/B is in the recursive set, or A is in the recursive set.

support.quote: if a WITH query is non-recursive and side-effect-free (that is, it is a SELECT containing no volatile functions) then it can be folded into the parent query, allowing joint optimization of the two query levels. By default, this happens if the parent query references the WITH query just once, but not if it references the WITH query more than once.
You can override that decision by specifying MATERIALIZED to force separate calculation of the WITH query, or by specifying NOT MATERIALIZED to force it to be merged into the parent query.
